industry.why: Underweight, one notch. Component 1 regime (rates-led late cycle: Richard's view 16-Sep-26, rates and yields rising, inflation high, consumer confidence low, downside skew; sources absent): advertising is the first spend cut when the consumer and corporates weaken. Relative strength F in both readings at industry and at its only sector. Counter-case: a ten-stock industry at F for two months is as likely mispriced as impaired.

sector.why: Underweight. Component 1 regime (rates-led late cycle: Richard's view 16-Sep-26, rates and yields rising, inflation high, consumer confidence low, downside skew; sources absent): advertising-funded content is cut first in a consumer squeeze. Relative strength AGREES, F both readings. Counter-case: ten stocks, as likely mispriced as impaired.

geography.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence for Underweight named and judged thin. Goldman Sachs (16 Oct) names 'worrying debt dynamics' in Finland alongside France, Belgium, Austria and Finland; that is one clause in one note with no spread reading, the same footing on which Ireland was held Neutral last week for Overweight, so the row does not move on it. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to D if a second source names Finland or a spread reading is read widening.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
